questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “Semaphores, mutexes, and deadlocks”?
options: A mutex protects a short critical section; a queue transfers values, so they solve different problems.
The scheduler runs tasks; `vTaskDelay` lets other work use the CPU.
Each task consumes stack; priority affects scheduler choices.
Start with a simple `loop()`; add tasks only for independent work with distinct timing needs.
questions.answer: A mutex protects a short critical section; a queue transfers values, so they solve different problems.
questions.explanation:
A mutex protects a short critical section; a queue transfers values, so they solve different problems.
Why: A semaphore coordinates events or a count of resources; a mutex protects shared mutable state and has ownership and priority-inheritance semantics. Hold a mutex briefly, release it around blocking I/O, and keep lock order consistent to reduce deadlock and priority-inversion risk. Never take a mutex from an ISR.

Start with a simple `loop()`; add tasks only for independent work with distinct timing needs.
